Breitling Is Making Super Chronomat Luxury Watches Exclusively for Aston Martin Valhalla Owners
10 photos
Photo: Aston Martin
Having enough resources to afford buying a million-dollar Aston Martin Valhalla puts one in a special class of our society. Not only in terms of wealth, but also when it comes to the love for cars and driving – after all, one really needs to be head over heels with such things, as the Valhalla has been designed to be driven rather than kept in a garage.
This special class of people also has access to perks not available to the rest of us, especially to stuff that relates directly to the design and extras that are to be fitted onto their vehicles. And they also draw the attention of other luxury brands that are after their money.
As you know, Aston Martin launched the Valhalla as its first-ever series-production, mid-engine PHEV supercar at the end of last year, with plans to make just 999 units of it. Each of them throws onto the road a combination of a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 engine and three electric motors, delivering together a maximum of 1,064 horsepower.
The Valhalla may be a series-production car, but by no means will the 999 units be all the same. Because this is the luxury world we’re talking about, buyers of this ride will have a pretty strong say in how their personal Valhalla will be specced.
And this is where Swiss watchmaker Breitling , the British carmaker’s official watch partner, comes in, ready to throw in a little extra to make Valhalla owners feel a bit more special.
The two companies announced this week that Breitling’s Super Chronomat collection of watches can be exclusively customized by each Valhalla owner to reflect not only their dreams, desires, likes, and passions, but also the hypercar they drive.
This is the first time the Swiss are opening the design process for one of their most high-profile collections, and they do this by launching a dedicated and off-the-grid configurator that can be accessed by owners.
There are two watches on the table for this: the Super Chronomat B19 44 Perpetual Calendar Chronograph and the Super Chronomat Automatic 38. The former comes with a 44 mm titanium case tied to a Rouleaux bracelet and features something its maker describes as one of the rarest combinations in the industry: an automatic perpetual calendar chronograph.
The Super Chronomat Automatic 38, on the other hand, features a 38 mm stainless-steel case and the same Rouleaux bracelet, with an automatic three-hand display taking center stage over the dial's technical pattern.
Neither Aston Martin nor Breitling said very much about the customization options available to buyers, other than the fact they can feature various colors and engravings. We also don’t know how much one costs (tens of thousands of dollars would probably be a safe bet), but, given the watches’ custom nature, that’s something for buyers alone to know.
